# Agent Instructions

All agent-facing instructions live in this file. `CLAUDE.md` contains only a
reference here. If you are a Claude Code agent, you have already loaded this
via `CLAUDE.md`. Other agents: read this file directly.

## Build and test

```bash
# Run unit tests (REQUIRED before every PR)
pip install pytest  # if not already installed
python3 -m pytest tests/ -v

# Validate imports
python3 -c "from runner import main"
python3 -c "from generate_results import generate_results_md"
python3 -c "from test_quality import compute_structural_metrics"
python3 -c "from llm_providers import get_provider"
python3 -c "from version_docs import build_doc, main"
python3 -c "from combine_results import combine"

# Regenerate all reports
python3 generate_results.py --all

# Run a benchmark (v4, all tasks/modes/models). Use 5 modes including
# powershell-tool. For multi-(model,effort) matrices, run sequentially via
# a wrapper script (see run-fresh-matrix-2026-05-06.sh).
python3 runner.py --tasks 11,12,13,15,16,17,18 --modes default,powershell,powershell-tool,bash,typescript-bun --models opus,sonnet

# Build per-CC-version reference docs in each run dir (system prompt +
# tool descriptions + sliced changelog). Idempotent; caches under
# .cache/cc-versions/.
python3 version_docs.py                   # all run dirs
python3 version_docs.py results/<run-dir> # one run

# Evaluate test quality (structural metrics only)
python3 test_quality.py results/2026-04-09_152435

# Evaluate test + deliverable quality with the default panel of judges
# (Haiku 4.5 via claude-cli + Gemini 3.1 Pro via gemini-cli). Each judge
# writes its own cache file: test-quality-{short}.json and
# deliverable-quality-{short}.json. 8-worker thread pool by default;
# bump `--workers` if your CLIs + account limits allow more concurrency.
python3 test_quality.py --llm-judge --deliverable-judge \
    --judges haiku45,gemini31pro --workers 8 results/2026-04-17_004319

# Re-evaluate with a single judge only (useful for bias cross-checks)
python3 test_quality.py --llm-judge --judges haiku45 results/2026-04-17_004319

# Build custom act container (optional, eliminates pwsh install overhead)
---

name: Environment Matrix Generator

# Trigger on code changes, PRs, a weekly schedule and manual dispatch so the
# matrix generator is continuously validated.
on:
  push:
  pull_request:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      config_file:
        description: 'Path to the matrix config JSON fixture'
        required: false
        default: 'fixtures/config.json'

# Least-privilege: the workflow only reads the repository.
permissions:
  contents: read

# CONFIG_FILE points at the fixture the generator consumes. The test harness
# overrides the file's contents per test case; the path stays constant.
env:
  CONFIG_FILE: ${{ github.event.inputs.config_file || 'fixtures/config.json' }}

jobs:
  test:
    name: Unit tests (Pester)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Run Pester unit tests
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          # Run the full Pester suite and fail the job on any test failure.
          $config = New-PesterConfiguration
          $config.Run.Path = './MatrixGenerator.Tests.ps1'
          $config.Run.Exit = $true
          $config.Output.Verbosity = 'Detailed'
          Invoke-Pester -Configuration $config

  generate:
    name: Generate build matrix
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: test
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Generate matrix from fixture
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $cfg = $env:CONFIG_FILE
          if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $cfg)) {
            throw "Config fixture not found: $cfg"
          }

          # Invoke the generator; it prints the matrix JSON to stdout.
          $json = ./MatrixGenerator.ps1 -ConfigPath $cfg
          Write-Host '----- BEGIN GENERATED MATRIX JSON -----'
          Write-Host $json
          Write-Host '----- END GENERATED MATRIX JSON -----'

          # Emit parseable, deterministic summary lines so the test harness can
          # assert on EXACT expected values from the act output.
          $obj = $json | ConvertFrom-Json
          Write-Host "GENERATED_MATRIX_SIZE=$($obj.size)"
          Write-Host "GENERATED_INCLUDE_COUNT=$(@($obj.matrix.include).Count)"
          Write-Host "GENERATED_FAIL_FAST=$($obj.'fail-fast')"
          if ($null -ne $obj.'max-parallel') {
            Write-Host "GENERATED_MAX_PARALLEL=$($obj.'max-parallel')"
          }

      - name: Publish matrix to step output
        id: matrix
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          # Demonstrate real-world use: expose the matrix as a job output that a
          # downstream job could consume via `strategy.matrix`.
          $json = ./MatrixGenerator.ps1 -ConfigPath $env:CONFIG_FILE
          $compact = ($json | ConvertFrom-Json).matrix | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 -Compress
          "matrix=$compact" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_OUTPUT -Append
          Write-Host "Published matrix output ($($compact.Length) chars)."

- **`MatrixGenerator.ps1`** — the generator.
